messages:
sophia: hey folks, quick heads-up: the cost dashboard is showing a negative prefetch savings for tenant t-7391 today. product flagged it. :grimacing:
cheng: saw that. morning ETL run had a schema change; suspect join/aggregation bug in the savings rollup
matt: can you paste the tenant id + a sample invocation? i'll pull request traces and the token_events rows
sophia: tenant t-7391, sample invocation id inv-84a3, route /v1/chat/generate. Dashboard shows savings -$12.34 which is obviously wrong
elaine: negative savings usually means we're either double-counting baseline or dropping the prefetched credit row and then computing base - actual wrong
ranj: two quick suspects: 1) inner join vs left join on prefetched_credits, 2) duplicate token_event produced when routing changed mid-invocation (prefetch + hotpath both recorded)
cheng: current dashboard SQL (simplified):
```
SELECT tenant, sum(baseline_cost) AS base, sum(actual_cost) AS actual, base - actual AS savings
FROM token_events
JOIN models m ON token_events.model_id = m.id
-- prefetched credits are in prefetched_credits table
GROUP BY tenant;
```
cheng: noticed prefetched_credits was recently moved to a separate materialized view; widget query still uses an inner join in a few places
matt: inner join would remove invocations w/o credits and can skew the base/actual if we later union prefetched tokens back in. also duplication on invocation_id would inflate baseline
sophia: the per-token rows in the econ panel look busted: baseline_tokens=1200, cached_tokens=800, net_billed_tokens=2000 (that net should be 400)
elaine: yep that's classic double-counting. UI-level group-by across a union of token rows will sum both rows if we don't dedupe by invocation_id
ranj: low-friction fix: dedupe by invocation_id and coalesce credits in the view. Longer-term: canonicalize prefetch credit to be a per-invocation attribute during ETL so UI queries are simpler
matt: i'll draft a hotfix query for the dashboard view to dedupe. Also add a unit test in ETL that asserts savings >= -1 for any tenant to catch regressions
cheng: suggested hotfix (staging):
```
WITH per_inv AS (
  SELECT invocation_id, tenant, sum(token_cost) AS baseline, sum(coalesce(prefetch_credit,0)) AS credit
  FROM token_events
  LEFT JOIN prefetched_credits USING (invocation_id)
  GROUP BY invocation_id, tenant
)
SELECT tenant, sum(baseline) AS base, sum(baseline - credit) AS actual, sum(baseline - (baseline - credit)) AS savings
FROM per_inv
GROUP BY tenant;
```
matt: looks good. two nits: 1) ensure prefetched_credits has unique invocation_id (de-dupe during join), 2) guard against negative credits (safety coalesce)
ranj: i'll run a quick smoke on staging for tenant t-7391 after you push
cost-bot: [smoke-run] kicking off staging smoke for tenant t-7391, checking daily rollup and per-invocation diffs. ETA ~90s
cost-bot: [smoke-run] done. staging rollup for tenant t-7391 shows savings +$11.87, per-invocation breakdown looks sane :white_check_mark:
sophia: amazing, thank you. can we gate shipping to prod on an alert rule that fires if any tenant's savings < -$1? product wants guardrails
matt: will file observability PR for an alert + pager owner (eng-platform + cost-reports). also adding an integration test in the ETL pipeline to assert no negative savings beyond tiny epsilon
cheng: i'll merge the SQL view change after a green canary and add a note in the econ schema doc explaining why we dedupe by invocation_id (so future devs don't remove it accidentally)
elaine: follow-up idea: tag token_events with route_version and prefer canonicalizing prefetched events to route "prefetch" so rollouts don't create ambiguous duplicates
sophia: sounds great. leaving this thread open until prod deploy passes. thanks y'all :heart:
